title: Knowledge check: Practical XPath Applications

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly covered in “Practical XPath Applications”?
questions.explanation: The attached XML curriculum lists “Extracting information from documents” under lesson 90, “Practical XPath Applications”. The other options are from different topics or unrelated areas.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the most reliable rule to remember when applying “Practical XPath Applications”?
options: XPath selects nodes or values; XSLT applies templates to transform a source tree; XQuery builds queries and results.
XPath is the same language as SQL in every XML database.
A browser HTML preview executes arbitrary XQuery.
Every transformation processor supports XSLT 3.0 streaming.
questions.answer_key: XPath selects nodes or values; XSLT applies templates to transform a source tree; XQuery builds queries and results.
questions.explanation: The correct choice separates the relevant XML concepts and avoids assumptions about processor behavior. Check the linked standard and actual implementation for details.

questions.prompt: After creating an example for “Practical XPath Applications”, what is the best next step?
options: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
Rely on visual appearance without parsing or validation.
Change several parts at once and infer the cause if the result changes.
questions.answer_key: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
questions.explanation: A small, reproducible test suite distinguishes expected behavior from a lucky example and makes version assumptions visible.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository; API GET responses expose only prompts/options and submit responses reveal feedback after grading.
